$comment: Design 123 §8.3 steering measurement. `grammar`: 20 prompts whose right answer is one of the nineteen new json-render grammars (5 lifecycles, 5 schemas, 5 plans/handoffs, 5 quantities); a pick is right when the reply's json-render elements include a type in `expect`. `hold`: 10 prompts whose right answer is prose, a Table, a Graph or a plain code block; a reply that draws any new grammar is a false draw. Bar: ≥ 16/20 and ≤ 1/10 (one re-tune of the prompt rows allowed).

grammar.prompt: Explain the lifecycle of an order in our shop: it starts as a cart, becomes placed when the customer pays, then packed, shipped and delivered; a placed or packed order can be cancelled, and a delivered one can be returned within 14 days.
What are the states a pull request goes through in GitHub, and what moves it between them? Include draft, review requested, changes requested, approved, merged and closed.
Walk me through the TCP connection states on the client side, from CLOSED through the handshake to ESTABLISHED and back through FIN_WAIT and TIME_WAIT.

Our background job runner has jobs that are queued, running, retrying (up to 3 times with backoff), failed or succeeded; a running job can also be cancelled by an operator. Describe how a job moves between these.
Describe the modes of a chat session in an agent harness: idle, running a turn, waiting for a tool approval, compacting context, and ended. What transitions exist and what guards them?
Design the database schema for a small blog: users, posts, comments and tags, with the keys and the relationships between the tables.
Show me the data model for an e-commerce order system: customers, orders, order lines, products and payments. Which fields are primary and foreign keys?

Sketch the class design for a notification service in TypeScript: an abstract Channel with send(), Email/SMS/Push implementations, a Notifier that composes channels, and a Template the Notifier depends on.
Propose SQLite tables for storing chat sessions, turns, tool calls and per-turn cost, with types, primary keys and the foreign keys between them.
Model a library system: members borrow copies of books; each book has authors; a loan has a due date and may be renewed. Give me the entities and how they relate.

Plan a four-week release: week 1 freeze and bug triage, weeks 1–2 QA regression, week 2–3 docs and release notes in parallel, week 3 release candidate, week 4 rollout after RC sign-off. Starting 2026-11-02.

Lay out a timeline for migrating our Postgres 13 cluster to 16: dual-write starts 2026-10-20 for a week, backfill the next week, read cutover depends on backfill, then decommission two weeks after cutover.

Describe our incident process across on-call engineer, incident commander and communications lead: who detects, who declares, who writes the status page update, who runs the postmortem, and where the handoffs are.

How does a change get to production here? Developer opens a PR, CI builds and tests, a reviewer approves, the release bot tags and deploys to staging, QA verifies, then ops promotes to prod. Show who does which step.

Explain our hiring pipeline across recruiter, hiring manager and the panel: sourcing, screen, take-home review, onsite, debrief, offer. Which role owns each step and where does the candidate get handed over?

Last week we spent $312 on Opus, $48 on Sonnet and $9 on Haiku. Opus went 60% to the design-123 session, 30% to bug triage and 10% to docs; Sonnet was all bug triage; Haiku was session titles. Show where the money went.
p95 latency per release: v1.0 410 ms, v1.1 380 ms, v1.2 290 ms, v1.3 305 ms, v1.4 240 ms; p50 was 120, 118, 95, 99, 80. Show the trend.
We started the year with 42 engineers, hired 12, lost 5 to attrition, moved 3 to the platform org and acquired a team of 4. Show how we got to the year-end number.
Signup conversion last month: 12,400 visited the pricing page, 3,100 started signup, 1,900 verified email, 640 created a workspace, 210 paid. Where do we lose people?
Test runs per day this week and how many failed: Mon 48/3, Tue 52/1, Wed 61/7, Thu 44/0, Fri 39/2. Give me the picture.

hold.prompt: What port does PostgreSQL listen on by default?
Give me the git command to delete a local branch that was already merged.
Compare SQLite, Postgres and DynamoDB for a small internal tool on setup effort, concurrency, query power and cost.

Explain the architecture of a typical three-tier web app: a browser talks to a load balancer, which fronts stateless API servers, which read and write a Postgres primary with a read replica and a Redis cache.
What is the difference between let and const in JavaScript?
Write a regular expression that matches an ISO 8601 date like 2026-10-07 and explain each part briefly.
How do I rotate an AWS IAM access key safely? Give me the steps.
Here is my nginx server block; tell me the three settings I should change for a production TLS site: server_name, listen 80, and no HSTS header.
Define these terms in one line each: idempotent, eventual consistency, backpressure, circuit breaker.
I renamed `parse_config` to `load_config` in three files and updated the two call sites. Anything else I should check before opening the PR?
